tasks.title: Promote the four staged migrations and regenerate DB types
tasks.dod: The four bot-connection migrations apply and revert cleanly on a fresh Postgres 16, the regenerated db.types.gen.ts compiles, and the migrations integration test rejects every constraint violation listed in the task.

tasks.title: Add platform primitives: bot error codes incl. the first 5xx, owner-guard message, config keys, Bot API root, secret-header redaction
tasks.dod: Unit tests prove the eight new error classes map to their codes, statuses and details (503 TELEGRAM_UNAVAILABLE not reported as INTERNAL_ERROR), config parses and validates the four new keys, the secret header is redacted, and the owner guard takes its message as a parameter with the team routes unchanged.

tasks.title: Build the scriptable fake Telegram Bot API and the webhook update builder for tests
tasks.dod: fake-telegram.test.ts shows grammY pointed at the fake through apiRoot receiving every scripted outcome (ok, unauthorized, transient, hang) with recorded call parameters, and the update builders validate against recorded Bot API examples.

tasks.title: Define the bots zod contracts in packages/shared
tasks.dod: Unit tests show every openapi.yaml example for the four owner operations parses with the shared bots schemas and that no schema accepts a token or webhook-secret field.

tasks.title: Implement the bots domain: token check, connection states, inbound filter, update normalisation, due rule
tasks.dod: Unit tests cover token trimming and format, the paste decision (connect, connect again, rotate, refuse with reason), every inbound-filter reason, every message kind incl. other, and the 3-minute due rule, with no I/O.

tasks.title: Implement the conversations and contacts domain rules: message kinds, edit rule, profile refresh
tasks.dod: Unit tests cover the edit rule with both tie-breaks and the redelivery case, the profile-refresh rule, and the 15-value message kind list, with no I/O.

tasks.title: Build the contacts module: repository with isolation tests, upsert-from-profile and count use cases
tasks.dod: Testcontainers tests prove every contacts repository method is isolated across two workspaces, a late older message never restores an old profile, and concurrent first upserts create one contact.

tasks.title: Build the conversation and message repositories with cross-workspace isolation tests
tasks.dod: Testcontainers tests prove every conversation and message repository method is isolated across two workspaces, duplicate inserts report already_present, and the conditional edit converges on the latest edit and ignores uncaptured messages.

tasks.title: Implement the conversations app layer: capture inbound message, apply edit, last message time, has conversations
tasks.dod: Unit and Postgres tests show capture creates contact, conversation and message in one transaction, stores a redelivery once, handles concurrent first messages and duplicates without doubles, applies only later edits, and leaves nothing half-written on a forced failure.

tasks.title: Build the bot repository, the AES-GCM token cipher and webhook secrets, with isolation tests incl. the two controlled exceptions
tasks.dod: Testcontainers tests prove every bot repository method and both controlled exceptions are isolated across two workspaces, the telegram_bot_id violation is reported without reading the other row, and the AES-GCM cipher round-trips without the token appearing in stored bytes.

tasks.title: Build the Telegram gateway: getMe, getWebhookInfo, setWebhook, deleteWebhook with typed outcomes and timeouts
tasks.dod: Integration tests against the fake Bot API show each gateway method returning its typed outcome (incl. a 1 s timeout as transient), setWebhook sending allowed_updates message/edited_message and max_connections, and no token or Bot API URL in errors or logs.

tasks.title: Implement the bots use cases get-settings and paste-token (connect, rotate, connect again, refusals, takeover confirmation)
tasks.dod: Unit tests with fakes cover every paste branch in the contract refusal order and the restore-on-setWebhook-failure path, getSettings makes no Telegram call, and a Postgres test shows two workspaces pasting the same bot concurrently yield one connection and one BOT_BELONGS_TO_ANOTHER_WORKSPACE.

tasks.title: Implement the bots use cases reconnect-with-stored-token and disconnect
tasks.dod: Unit and integration tests cover every branch of reconnect (flow 6) and disconnect (flow 7), including needs_token on a rejected stored token, the row kept when conversations exist and deleted otherwise, and no deleteWebhook for a foreign URL.

tasks.title: Implement the bots use case accept-webhook-update: secret check, inbound filter, capture epoch, hand-off to conversations
tasks.dod: Unit tests cover unauthorized, captured, already-present, edited and every ignore reason, and a Postgres test shows one person writing to two workspaces' bots gets a separate contact and conversation in each.

tasks.title: Implement the scheduled health check: run-health-check use case and the bots.schedule-health-checks / bots.check-health jobs
tasks.dod: Unit tests cover each row of the events.md outcome table, and pg-boss integration tests show one check per bot at a time and a no-op for a disconnected bot or a mismatched workspace id.

tasks.title: Expose the owner-only bot routes and wire the bots, conversations and contacts modules into buildDeps / buildApp
tasks.dod: app.inject() tests show the four owner routes returning every contract status and code, 403 "Only business owners manage the bot" for an operator, 404 for a non-member or another workspace's owner, no Telegram call on GET, and no token in any response.

tasks.title: Expose the Telegram webhook route with secret-before-parse, empty-body 401/200 and fail-closed 500
tasks.dod: app.inject() tests show the webhook capturing every kind, edit, redelivery and ordering case, ignoring filtered updates with 200, refusing every forgery with an identical empty 401, and answering 500 on a forced DB failure followed by a single capture on redelivery.

tasks.title: Register the health-check workers in buildApp and prove five-minute freshness over a simulated hour
tasks.dod: buildApp() registers the health-check workers and a simulated-hour integration test shows no live bot ever more than 5 minutes stale, with revoke and takeover detected on the first due tick.

tasks.dod: The three API-level e2e stories (capture lifecycle, edits and redeliveries, health and recovery) pass against an ephemeral database and the fake Bot API, each step using only what earlier steps returned.
